description.narrative: The proposed Finance Sector Development Program will help the Government of Vanuatu to achieve an inclusive and resilient finance sector that can support private sector-led recovery in Vanuatu. The program will support policy and institutional reforms for financial inclusion, compliance with anti-money laundering (AML), countering the financing of terrorism (CFT), countering proliferation financing (CPF) and exchange of information standards, and improving the business environment for private sector-led recovery and growth. The program will strengthen women's access to financial services and contribute to financial system resilience by facilitating infrastructure to increase access to and use of digital financial services.

2.1. To facilitate the use of technology in customer due diligence processes of financial institutions, the Financial Intelligence Unit undertook a diagnostic report to examine the suitability of the existing legal and regulatory framework, as the basis for further reforms, for use of technology.

2.2. To support the online registration of identities from remote locations, the Department of Civil Registration and Identity Management established an updated identity database and confirm accuracy, completeness, and compliance with established standards.

2.3. To facilitate a conducive environment for data-sharing between the private and public sectors, the government issued a policy to ensure data privacy and security, which will comply with global standards

2.4. To support the international exchange of information on request, the Minister of Finance and Economic Management approved and gazetted regulations under the Tax Administration Act to establish a framework for the exchange of information on beneficial owners of legal entities with competent authorities internationally

3.1. To facilitate trade and growth in business opportunities, the Ministry of Trade and Commerce: (i) established a platform for businesses' online submission and payments for import and export certificates, licenses, and permits, and (ii) issues certificates of origin online
3.2. To facilitate the development of commerce and industry, the Ministry for Trade, and Commerce approved an e-commerce strategy with women's empowerment included in the strategic framework.

4.1. To manage disaster risks and support sustainable financing, the Council of Ministers approved: (i) The National Disaster Risk Finance Policy 2024-2029 that lays the policy framework to enhance the financial protection of Vanuatu against disasters; and (ii) a framework for the issuance of sustainable bonds, which outlines how bonds could finance projects that deliver environmental and social benefits, including to address climate change, in Vanuatu.
